question: What constitutes the real estate sector in Uganda and how are operators categorized across the value chain?
answer: Real estate in Uganda comprises land, buildings, and attached immovable structures, organized across four primary market segments: 1) Land — undeveloped vacant property acquired, partitioned, rezoned, or sold; 2) Residential Real Estate — single-family houses, apartments, condominiums, and housing estates; 3) Commercial Real Estate — shopping malls, office complexes, arcades, and hospitality facilities; 4) Industrial Real Estate — warehouses, logistics hubs, and manufacturing plants. Key industry players include Land Dealers (acquire land for raw resale), Land Developers (partition, open access roads, extend water/power, and rezone land), Property Developers (buy, build, or renovate properties for sale), Property Managers (manage tenancies, maintain buildings, and collect rent on behalf of landlords), Real Estate Agents (licensed by the Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development to represent buyers and sellers), and Landlords.

question: How are real estate companies and sole proprietor property dealers taxed on sales of land and buildings in Uganda?
answer: Under the Income Tax Act and the Real Estate Sector Guide (FY 2025-26): 1) Corporate Real Estate Dealers (e.g. Kato Investments Ltd): Taxed at 30% Corporation Income Tax (CIT) on net chargeable profits (Total sales of land and buildings minus Cost of Sales minus allowable operating expenses, employee benefits, billboard advertising, media publicity, utilities, administrative overheads, and debt interest); 2) Individual Sole Proprietor Dealers (e.g. Nest Property Uganda): Taxed under resident individual graduated income tax rates up to 40% on net business profits (chargeable income above UGX 120,000,000 annually attracts UGX 35,406,000 + 40% on excess); 3) Presumptive Tax Exclusion: Real estate developers and commercial property dealers are excluded from presumptive tax and must maintain full books of accounts; 4) Form DT-1001: Provisional returns must be submitted twice yearly.

question: What are the VAT rules on sales of unimproved land versus commercial real estate in Uganda?
answer: Under the Value Added Tax Act: 1) Supply of Unimproved Land: The sale, lease, or transfer of raw, unimproved land is strictly an EXEMPT supply under the Second Schedule of the VAT Act (no VAT is charged); 2) Commercial Real Estate & Serviced Plots: The sale, lease, or letting of commercial buildings, shopping malls, arcades, industrial warehouses, or serviced plots with infrastructure is a standard-rated taxable supply attracting 18% VAT; 3) Compulsory Registration: Real estate dealers with annual taxable turnover exceeding UGX 150 million (or UGX 37.5M in 3 consecutive months) must register for VAT; 4) Residential Accommodations: Long-term lease or letting of residential dwellings for human habitation is exempt from VAT.

question: What tax obligations apply to property managers and real estate agents in Uganda?
answer: Under URA guidelines at https://ura.go.ug/en/property-management/ and https://ura.go.ug/en/real-estate-agents-ac/: 1) Property Managers: Act as managing agents between property owners and tenants. Rent collected by a property manager is a statutory pass-through paid to the landlord and is not recognized as revenue of the management firm; however, property management fees and commissions earned are taxable business revenue subject to 30% CIT (or individual income tax) and 18% VAT if registered; 2) Real Estate Agents: Licensed by the Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development (MLHUD), commissions earned on sales, purchases, and letting of land/buildings attract 18% VAT and 6% Withholding Tax on agency contracts exceeding UGX 1,000,000; 3) EFRIS: All real estate agency fees and management commissions must be billed via EFRIS.

question: What Stamp Duty rates and local authority deductions apply to land and property transactions?
answer: Under the Stamp Duty Act and Real Estate Sector Guide: 1) Property & Land Transfers: 1.5% of the market value determined by the Chief Government Valuer (CGV) on land transfer forms; 2) Commercial Leases: 1% of the total rental value over the full lease term; 3) Mortgages & Debentures: 0.5% of the secured loan amount; 4) Industrial Park Exemption: Developers of Industrial Parks or Free Zones enjoy Nil Stamp Duty on debentures, land leases, land transfers, share capital increases, and feasibility/construction agreements; 5) Local Authority Charges: Ground rent, property rates, environmental taxes, and municipal operating fees paid to KCCA or local town councils are fully deductible operational expenses under income tax.
